source.title: Escaping Local Minima Provably in Non-convex Matrix Sensing: A Deterministic Framework via Simulated Lifting
source.authors: Tianqi Shen; Jin-Ji Yang; Jun He; Kunhan Gao; Ze-Yu Zheng; Zi-Ye Ma

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no truncation apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper includes an illustrative neural-network training experiment that measures training loss and explicitly reports baseline GD and SGD stalling at nonzero loss, as well as outcomes after an added escape method. It does not test the benchmark classification-error recipes in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's main matrix-sensing results and cited findings about deep learning are not rows for the claim. The neural-network experiment in Section 6.3 measures training loss in a quadratic network on Iris, so it bears on V1's training-convergence behavior but does not measure classification error or benchmark datasets. Alternative escape-search comparisons are excluded because they evaluate methods added after GD stagnates, not training from random initialization as claimed.
record.test_reason: The study tests deterministic escape methods for matrix sensing and a quadratic network on Iris. None of its results tests V1–V6: training loss in this network does not establish CIFAR convolutional-network classification error, and no experiment tests the specified width, depth, initialization, stability-threshold, or normalization comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes Section 6.3: the Iris experiment is a proof of concept for SOD escape, with broader neural-network applications proposed as future work. The paper's principal conclusion concerns conditional escape guarantees and empirical recovery improvements in matrix sensing, rather than general neural-network convergence.
record.recipe_differences: The neural-network experiment uses a quadratic network on Iris and compares training-loss dynamics; it does not reproduce the benchmark classification-error studies or their training recipes. SOD is an added escape procedure activated after stagnation.
record.method_sensitivity: Training behavior differs by optimizer: GD and SGD stagnate at nonzero training loss, while Adam decreases loss gradually; adding SOD after GD stagnation produces a sharp drop.

fits_no_version.finding: On the Iris quadratic-network task, GD and SGD stall at positive training loss, Adam decreases loss gradually, and adding SOD after GD stagnation produces an immediate loss reduction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structured escape directions can improve training-loss optimization after gradient methods stagnate in a quadratic neural network.

fits_no_version.finding: The study derives conditional deterministic escape guarantees and reports improved recovery success with SOD in matrix-sensing experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Simulated tensor lifting can supply deterministic escape steps for spurious solutions in certain factorized matrix-sensing problems.

record.problems: The neural-network experiment is explicitly illustrative and uses a single Iris binary-classification task with a one-hidden-layer quadratic network. The supplied text gives qualitative loss descriptions without numeric values, uncertainty estimates, or stated initialization details; it reports training loss rather than classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results meeting the row rule were identified. Figure 12 panel (b) compares escape-search methods after GD stagnates; these are evaluations of added escape strategies, not the training behavior named by the claim. Matrix-sensing experiments concern a different task and objective.

untested.parts: All parts: sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, training classification error under SGD or Adam from random initialization, corrupted labels, and size or regularization qualifications.
ReLU teacher-student local-minimum frequencies and the effect of adding one or two student neurons.
Depth degradation in plain convolutional networks and prevention by identity shortcuts, including the initialization and normalization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, training speed, and trainable depth.
Recovery above initial stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability training, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup alternative.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V1 limits_scope verdict. A different network and a different outcome measure do not supply a scope limitation on V1. Matrix-sensing equivalence to quadratic-network training also does not establish the ReLU teacher-student width effect in V2.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, convolutional networks, corrupted or random labels, model size, initialization, or training classification error. The experiment uses a quadratic network on Iris and reports training loss.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiments and the effect of student width relative to teacher width are not tested.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks, depth, shortcuts, and normalization are not tested.
Activation-matched initializations, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth are not tested.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature, loss dynamics above the threshold, and divergence are not tested.
Batch normalization, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup are not tested.

rows.subject: one-hidden-layer quadratic neural network (QNN)
rows.operation_detail: Standard gradient descent on the binary Iris classification training task, before applying SOD escape.

conditions.value: within the plotted iterations; exact count not stated

rows.value: GD stagnates at a nonzero training loss
rows.note: Authors state that GD stagnates at nonzero training loss; no numeric loss value or training classification error is given.
rows.check: Nonzero training loss for a quadratic network on Iris cannot determine V1's training classification error in sufficiently large CIFAR convolutional networks. The reported stagnation is accurate; Figure 12's iteration axis extends to 14,000.

rows.subject: one-hidden-layer quadratic neural network (QNN)
rows.operation_detail: Stochastic gradient descent on the binary Iris classification training task.

conditions.value: within the plotted iterations; exact count not stated

rows.value: SGD stagnates at a nonzero training loss
rows.note: Authors report nonzero-loss stagnation; the text does not state the initialization or a numeric loss.
rows.check: SGD stagnation is reported accurately, but the system, dataset, and measure do not match V1. Nonzero loss does not establish nonzero classification error. Figure 12's iteration axis extends to 14,000.

rows.subject: one-hidden-layer quadratic neural network (QNN)
rows.operation_detail: Adam optimization on the binary Iris classification training task.

conditions.value: many additional iterations; exact count not stated

rows.note: Text reports gradual decrease, not whether Adam reaches zero loss.
rows.check: Gradual loss reduction does not establish whether Adam reaches near-zero classification error, and the Iris quadratic network falls outside V1's system and dataset.

rows.subject: one-hidden-layer quadratic neural network (QNN)
rows.operation_detail: Apply SOD escape once GD stagnation is detected, then continue training.
rows.baseline: GD stagnates at nonzero training loss; Adam reaches the stated loss level only after many additional iterations
rows.value: SOD escape produces a sharp drop in training loss; loss level reached in one escape step
rows.note: The outcome is for a deliberately applied escape step after detected stagnation; it is not evidence about unmodified gradient training from random initialization. No numeric loss or training classification error is stated.
rows.check: This evaluates the study's added SOD escape method after stagnation. It should not be a claim-testing row: neither its training procedure nor its system, dataset, and loss measure tests V1.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
